funding.provides: The Employment Training Panel reimburses California companies that train employees for high-skill, high-wage jobs.
funding.how_to_apply: See the ETP fact sheet (DE 8714N) for how to apply

funding.name: California Division of Apprenticeship Standards: How to Become an Apprentice
funding.provider: California Department of Industrial Relations, Division of Apprenticeship Standards (DAS)
funding.provides: DAS page on how to become a registered apprentice; apprenticeship programs are paid earn-while-you-learn training, and the page links to the apprenticeship program search and wage lookup.
funding.eligibility: Page states educational requirements vary by program (some require a high school diploma or equivalent, others have more rigorous standards, and some have none); some programs require an aptitude or other test; most programs require English proficiency. Qualities of successful apprentices listed: perseverance, ambition, initiative.
funding.how_to_apply: Not stated as an application; the page links to the Find an apprenticeship program, Find a registered apprentice and Find apprenticeship wages tools on the DAS site.

funding.name: California Opportunity Youth Apprenticeship (COYA) Grant
funding.provider: California Department of Industrial Relations, Division of Apprenticeship Standards (DAS)
funding.provides: Grants to develop and test practices that increase participation of opportunity youth in pre-apprenticeship and apprenticeship programs, delivered through community-based organizations and partners.
funding.eligibility: Target is opportunity youth, defined on the page as ages 16 to 24 who are at risk of or disconnected from education or employment, unhoused, in child welfare, juvenile justice or criminal legal systems, living in concentrated poverty, or facing barriers to labor market participation (grantees must show proof). Sector: programs serving occupations outside the building and construction trades (the page says building trades within California Apprenticeship Council jurisdiction are not covered; fire trades programs may apply with CAC approval). Eligible applicants must be mission-driven community-based organizations with at least 2 years serving opportunity youth. Round 3 awardees announced April 2026 (performance period 2026-2028).
funding.amount: Up to $6,000 per pre-apprentice for an educational stipend during pre-apprenticeship training (100% to the pre-apprentice; not a wage supplement). Round 3 continuation grants total $13.2 million.
funding.how_to_apply: Not stated on the page for individuals; the page lists the COYA grantee list (Round 1, 2 and 3 PDFs) and DAS grant solicitations.

funding.name: Equal Representation in Construction Apprenticeship (ERiCA) Grant
funding.provider: California Department of Industrial Relations, Division of Apprenticeship Standards (DAS)
funding.provides: Funding to increase equitable access to building and construction career pathways for women, non-binary individuals and underrepresented populations, including childcare support and outreach to underserved populations.
funding.eligibility: Page describes the program as serving women, non-binary individuals and underrepresented populations in construction apprenticeship; eligibility rules for individuals are not stated on the page.
funding.amount: DAS awarded $26,169,217 for ERiCA Program Year 2025-27 (performance period June/July 2025 to June 30, 2027); first round awarded $25 million (PY 2023-2025).
funding.how_to_apply: Not stated on the page beyond grant program information; see DAS grant pages.

funding.name: Apprenticeship Innovation Funding (AIF)
funding.provider: California Department of Industrial Relations, Division of Apprenticeship Standards (DAS)
funding.provides: Funding for new and innovative registered apprenticeship programs in sectors overseen by the Interagency Advisory Committee on Apprenticeship (healthcare, transportation, education, advanced manufacturing, information technology and others outside the building and fire trades); not a competitive grant.
funding.eligibility: Apprenticeship programs associated with IACA-overseen occupations that meet the eligibility criteria on the page (includes both new and existing programs).
funding.amount: Not stated on the page beyond reimbursement model; the page cites past awardee highlights.
funding.how_to_apply: Submissions for AIF reimbursement open once per year and consider active apprentices supported and trained within the previous year.
